{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Challenging corporate control of the media is essential to restoring democratic discourse and resisting corporate power.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The American people collectively own the airwaves, with an estimated access value of $750 billion.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The public receives virtually nothing in return for spectrum licenses the FCC grants for free to corporate broadcasters.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Regulatory palliatives, including the public interest doctrine, have been eviscerated.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Public television and radio are co-opted.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Community voices are marginalized.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Trust busting is needed to break up media monopolies where one corporation can simultaneously control radio, television, newspaper, and cable service in a single media market.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Federal dollars in the form of grants or small business loans can go to nonprofits looking to start local newspapers, cable stations, low-watt radio stations, and even satellite radio connections.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The federal government should fulfill its commitment to expanding and modernizing the Internet the way it did in funding the U.S. highway system and rural electrification.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Any future rollouts of high speed connectivity should be available in every community, regardless of income or population concentration.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
